Simulating startup trajectories & multi-agent decision-making — validation review

Project 74 · 2026-09-01 · branch review-3 @ e205da7

All numbers VERIFIED/EXECUTED from data on disk; nothing synthetic.

CSimulator — important validation gaps
BAgents — evidence of policy value with important limitations

1 · Problem and system

The simulator is a monthly SaaS-startup environment: revenue, cash, churn, pricing, macro shocks; an episode ends at bankruptcy or the time limit.

The agent layer is a boardroom of rule-based C-suite proposals, steered by an LLM "oracle brief" through a fixed ActionModifier, with episodic memory retrieved from past runs.

The two claims defended (validation_plan.md §1):

  • (S) the environment reproduces the scale-free regularities of real SaaS well enough to be a credible testbed.
  • (P) the agent layer makes economically sensible decisions that causally improve simulated outcomes over trivial and rule-based controls.
Pipeline (existing text diagram from system_audit.md) 
INPUTS  seed s, initial_config (defaults: MRR $50k, cash $1M, CAC $50, price $50,
        product_quality 0.1, headcount 1)                    [env/startup_env.py:140-164]
   │
STATE   EnvState: 16 monthly variables (see §2)              [env/schemas.py:5-47]
   │
OBSERVE Policies receive the FULL EnvState object, not the gym observation vector.
        run_simulation calls agent.get_action(env.state)     [simulation_runner.py:358]
        (the Box observation space at startup_env.py:108-111 is dead weight for every
        policy in the repo — nothing consumes _get_obs())
   │
RETRIEVE (oracle_v3/v4 modes only, on refresh months) trend context from a 5-month
        deque + ≤3 Chroma memories filtered to the CURRENT run_id + (v4_causal, under
        active shock) Neo4j graph context                     [oracle/oracle.py:117-171]
   │
DECIDE  Boardroom: 3 rule-based C-suite proposals → scored → composed into one
        ActionBundle → ActionModifier scales it by the LLM brief → sanity bounds →
        dynamic minimum floors → cash-conflict resolver        [boardroom/boardroom.py:109-326]
   │
PARSE   ActionAdapter.translate_action clamps/typos-proofs the bundle
        (spend ≥ 0, hires ≥ 0, price change clamped to [-0.5, +1.0])  [agents/adapter.py]
   │
STEP    StartupEnv.step: shocks → cascade/hysteresis/recovery → marketing Hill response
        → expansion → R&D → churn → MRR update → cash update → pricing → hiring clip →
        burn subtraction → CAC/LTV update → Rule-of-40 → reward   [env/startup_env.py:168-289]
   │
OUTCOME terminated = cash ≤ 0; truncated = 120 months. Per-episode metrics
        (final MRR/cash, survival, avg Rule-of-40, recovery events) [simulation_runner.py:459-498]

2 · The dataset

EDGAR is the calibration and validation benchmark; all agent experience data is simulator-generated.

Dataset card (data/DATASET_CARD.md, frozen)

Dataset card — EDGAR SaaS quarterly panel (frozen)

Consolidates data/coverage_report.md (screening, generated 2026-08-26) and

validation/edgar_data_audit.md (capability audit, 2026-08-30). Card written

2026-09-01. **This panel is the project's calibration and validation benchmark;

all agent experience data is simulator-generated, never drawn from this panel.**

Source and construction

  • Source: SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL API (cached responses in

data/cache/edgar/, 41 CIKs; no network needed to regenerate).

  • Pipeline: data/ingest_edgar.py → data/edgar.db (tables companies,

facts) → data/edgar_facts.csv (long form) and data/edgar_ratios.csv

(per company-quarter, the analysis panel).

  • Q4 handling: filers report Q4 only cumulatively; Q4 rows are recovered by

exact differencing of two filed year-to-date figures (24.4% of fact values,

each row carrying derivation + derived_from). Nothing is imputed,

interpolated or forward-filled. WHERE derivation IS NULL restricts to

strictly as-filed values.

Inclusion criteria (declared before screening)

1. Reports SellingAndMarketingExpense separately from G&A (filers reporting

only combined SG&A are excluded — S&M is not recoverable from XBRL).

2. Uses a standard revenue tag (RevenueFromContractWithCustomer…).

3. Has ≥16 consecutive quarters with revenue, R&D and S&M all present.

Screened 41 candidates → 39 included, 2 excluded (MNDY: non-standard tags;

PAYC: SG&A combined only).

Coverage

  • Companies (39): QLYS EGHT PCTY RPD TWLO BL YEXT BAND ALRM RNG TENB WK

APPF ZS DOMO ESTC MDB OKTA CRWD FSLY PD ZM DDOG NET SPT ASAN AI DOCN KLTR

PATH ZETA AMPL FRSH INTA S WEAV BRZE GTLB KVYO

  • Quarter range: 2010Q2–2026Q2. Complete core quarters (revenue + QoQ

growth + S&M% + R&D% all present): 1,288 (1,473 company-quarter rows in

edgar_ratios.csv, 1,332 with revenue).

  • Frequency: quarterly. Simulator output is aggregated to quarters for any

comparison; no monthly EDGAR series exists or is fabricated.

Fields

Seven directly ingested concepts (rows / companies in facts): revenue

1,332/39 · sm_expense 1,391/39 · rnd_expense 1,395/39 · ga_expense 1,385/39 ·

cost_of_revenue 1,303/39 · cash 1,452/39 · operating_cash_flow 1,292/39

(plus short_term_investments 442/20).

Derived quantities used in validation (in edgar_ratios.csv): QoQ revenue

growth, S&M % of revenue, R&D % of revenue (together: discretionary spend

intensity), gross margin, magic number, burn multiple, Rule of 40,

cash-and-investments.

What this panel can / cannot validate

Can validate (used in)Cannot validate (declared, not forced)
Revenue-growth distribution, persistence, volatility, deceleration with scale (E1–E3, E5)Churn, CAC, LTV, customer counts (not in XBRL; ChartMogul benchmarks give range checks only)
Spend structure: S&M%, R&D% of revenue (E4)Price/ARPU levels or pricing actions
Gross margin range (E7b)Product quality; any monthly dynamics
Drawdown/recovery shape of revenue (E6)Hiring at quarterly resolution (headcount is annual 10-K prose)
Real-state initialization for the counterfactual backtest (C1); observational allocation direction (C2)Macro block (rates, unemployment, confidence — out of EDGAR scope)

Known biases: survivor-biased, right-tail population (successful post-IPO

SaaS; smallest observed quarter ≈ $15.8M revenue, two orders of magnitude above

the simulator's $50k-MRR anchor) — all comparisons are therefore scale-free;

absolute dollars are never compared.

5 · What does not work, and why

Revenue drawdowns: simulator vs reality (report §5b, E6 — exploratory)

PanelEpisodes/100 quartersMedian depthRecovery rateMedian recovery
EDGAR (39 companies)3.011%85%3 quarters
Sim boardroom (75 episodes)1.661%0%—
Sim oracle_v31.463%2%10 quarters

Memory ablation simulator-internal

Episodic retrieval adds +$37.9k final MRR (95% CI [+$14.0k, +$66.3k], p=0.0023) — 3.2% of the oracle layer's gain over the boardroom. The brief mechanism, not memory, carries the value.

Observational check against real companies

C2 — Allocation-direction consistency: NULL. 97 stress company-quarters (growth < panel p25, spend intensity > median; 25 companies): improved and lagged halves show statistically indistinguishable allocation-intensity changes (p = 0.65 S&M, 0.86 R&D); directionally, improvers *grew* absolute S&M and R&D (+6%) while lagged companies held or cut — the opposite of the agent's cut-marketing stress response. Observational, survivor-biased, mechanically coupled to growth, and unadjusted for company clustering — so this is recorded as *absence of observational support*, not a refutation (validation/results/c2_allocation_consistency.csv).

Diagnosis (from the C1 scorecard row): scale-aware marketing curve too generous at real-company spend intensity; SATURATION_ACQUISITION_RATE=0.20/mo (the one ASSUMED free parameter) is falsified as too high; also no financing mechanism (6 high-burn companies die in-sim that in reality raised capital)

Do not claim

v4 ≠ v3; reward improvements; retrieval as the main source of value (it contributes ≈3% of the oracle gain); any real-world agent value; any real-company forecast.

6 · Defensible claims (report §8, verbatim)

Simulator. "At its calibration scale, the environment reproduces the quarterly revenue-growth distribution (median within the EDGAR panel's IQR) and the growth-deceleration-with-scale regularity of 39 public SaaS companies (1,288 quarters), while exhibiting higher persistence and volatility than the panel and far deeper, non-recovering revenue drawdowns under its injected shocks; initialized from real company states it over-projects four-quarter growth (median error ≈ +50 pp), so it serves as a controlled comparative testbed rather than a forecasting model."

Agents. "Under matched random worlds, the boardroom policy improves final MRR over no-action, random and heuristic controls (paired Hedges g 0.60–0.82, n=50), and the LLM-oracle layer improves it further in 74–75 of 75 paired episodes (g ≈ 0.93, p < 1e-13), with the gain concentrated in post-shock periods — all effects are simulator-internal and are reported as model-based counterfactuals."

7 · Next step — autonomous agent workflow

run_simulation already runs 120-month episodes unattended end-to-end (environment, boardroom, oracle briefs, memory writes) with no human in the loop.

Post-review work: expose an auto-run mode in the product frontend — launch a policy, stream the monthly trace live, with an optional human-in-the-loop override on the composed action before each step.

Appendix

The eleven questions (report §7)

Realistic enough as a controlled environment?

Qualified yes at research scale for *comparative* policy experiments (E1/E3 pass; E2/E5/E4 documented); no as a predictive model (C1).

Do agent actions affect outcomes?

Yes — causally, with per-lever magnitudes quantified (A1).

Are decisions economically sensible?

Rule layer yes (10/10); LLM layer partially — trend/shock-sensitive, level-blind (A4).

Do agents beat simple controls?

Yes, in-sim, paired, medium-to-large effects (A2; A3 recorded-paired).

Does retrieval/context improve decisions?

Briefs are predictive (+17 pp, A6i); retrieval changes ~60% of monthly spend decisions and yields a small, significant outcome gain (+$37.9k, CI [+14.0k, +66.3k], 15/20 seeds) — ≈3% of the oracle layer's total value; the brief mechanism, not memory, carries the bulk.

Robust across seeds/states?

Yes: 74–75/75 recorded seeds, 20/20 replicated under clean RNG, and the boardroom ranking holds in 9/9 initial-condition cells (A7) with paired g 0.64–0.84 throughout.

Real-state initialization — agent beats controls?

No. Increment negative everywhere; see §5.

Simulated vs observed real trajectories?

Simulation over-projects growth by ~45–50 pp per 4 quarters at real scale.

Which conclusions are empirical?

The EDGAR panel statistics; the claim audit; brief-label distributions; all paired in-sim comparisons *as statements about the simulator*.

Which depend on simulator-based counterfactuals?

Every "agent adds value" statement (A2, A3, C1 arms) — value is defined inside the model's dynamics.

What remains unvalidated?

Churn/CAC/price/product-quality realism, macro block, monthly dynamics, hiring, v4 causal-graph contribution. (Moved to validated since the first draft: retrieval outcome-increment — small positive; robustness grid — PASS; candidate regret and drawdown/recovery — exploratory results in §5b; allocation-direction consistency — null.)
